said on Wednesday that it plans to create 6K jobs across the U.S., including 2K in Texas, to expand advanced manufacturing and accelerate munitions production.
The company is investing $300M to expand its Grand Prairie, Texas, facility to more than 735K square feet.
Hadrian will install a 24-machine automated machining cell at the facility, expected to become operational in early 2027.
The company also expects to add nearly 100 advanced machines at the site by the end of 2026.
The expansion supports production of key defense systems, including PAC-3 MSE, THAAD, PrSM, and JATM.
The investment is part of Lockheed Martin’s broader $8B–$9B plan through 2030 to expand over 20 U.S. facilities.

title: Lockheed Martin plans 6K U.S. jobs in $300M Texas expansion
